title: ADHD in Adults: Recognition, Diagnosis, and Treatment
description: ADHD isn't just a childhood condition. How adult ADHD presents differently, getting diagnosed as an adult, and treatment options that actually work.

content.text: You weren't the hyperactive kid bouncing off walls. But you lose your keys constantly, can't finish projects, and your mind never stops. Could it be ADHD? For millions of adults, the answer is yes.
Adult ADHD often looks different from the childhood stereotype:

items: Difficulty with focus manifests as missing deadlines, forgetting appointments
Impulsivity shows up in interrupting, impulsive purchases, job-hopping
Time blindness—consistently late, underestimating how long things take
High intelligence can mask symptoms through compensation
Women present differently (more inattentive, less hyperactive)
Childhood was structured enough to cope
Review of childhood history (symptoms must have started before age 12)
Rule out other conditions (sleep disorders, thyroid, depression)

content.text: Online ADHD assessments can suggest ADHD but cannot diagnose it. You need evaluation by a qualified professional—psychiatrist, psychologist, or specialized NP.

items: Non-stimulants (Strattera, Wellbutrin): Options if stimulants don't work
Medication is highly effective but not a complete solution
Working with your brain, not against it

content.text: Adult ADHD is real, common, and treatable. If you've always felt like you're working twice as hard for half the results, and these symptoms resonate, it's worth getting evaluated. Diagnosis can be life-changing—not as a label, but as an explanation and a path to effective treatment.
